summary:
Receipt and disposition are different facts. A successful comment cursor proves a bounded read, not that its message body was understood or acted on. Reconcile unseen messages and edited bodies against the last successful cursor before claiming a channel is processed. In the primary owning issue, give each substantive message and each distinct scope its disposition: Ack means read and understood; Assigned names the accountable owner, next action and next checkpoint; Resolved names the independently verified scope and evidence. A message can resolve one scope while another remains assigned or held. Acknowledgment, a worker report and a cursor advance do not prove a native effect or acceptance. Keep this in the existing primary thread, without a new mandatory ledger.

Prepare the complete applicable runtime path before an export depends on it, including setup/helpers, storage and temporary paths, resource enforcement, observation, cleanup and final retention. Prepare a later gate in parallel when its inputs and write domains are independent; do not make a useful source preparation wait on an unrelated operation. Preserve reserved input stability, supplier bounds, existing holds and original failure/Unknown outcomes. Advance a selected finite sequence on verified success under its original clocks; complete already admitted steps without repeated confirmation, but never auto-retry an uncertain effect or renew its clock. An unqualified next dependency remains a named gap, not permission to bypass the supplying owner.

A review-ready successor identifies the accepted baseline and its scope, changed files, affected dependencies, relevant test results and remaining gaps. Reuse unchanged verified bytes and historical evidence only for their proven scope. Refresh determining head/base, policy, workflow, credential, runtime and capacity facts when they change. Test counts, source CI, byte receipts and helper success do not establish native runtime, export or consumer qualification.

For the current runner delivery chain, useful completion gates are runtime qualified, export qualified, bake completed, registered and first BAR passed. Report each actual result or precise missing proof rather than a percentage. These are this chain's example gates, not a new lifecycle imposed on every delivery. Public primary [4778](https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4778) retains whole acceptance; a scoped [Root disposition](https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6420461806) illustrates retaining a held source finding without accepting the whole runtime. This record captures the accepted coordination decision, changes no rule/helper or operation authority, and supplies no runtime acceptance.
title: Distinguish message receipt, scoped disposition and actual runtime completion gates
